text: The library closes at six o’clock on weekdays.
tip: Link "closes" to "at six" — do not pause before the time.

text: Students must bring their own calculators to the exam.
tip: Keep "must bring" together as one phrase.

text: Coffee prices have risen sharply since the beginning of 2022.
The museum offers free entry to students on Sundays.
tip: "free entry" is one unit; say it smoothly.

text: Although the report is long, its conclusions are surprisingly clear.
tip: Do not pause after "long" — the clause continues.

text: Researchers tested the new drug on more than two thousand volunteers.
tip: Say "more than" as one unit before the number.

text: Rainfall in the region has decreased steadily over the last decade.
tip: Link "has decreased" smoothly; avoid stopping mid-phrase.

text: Travellers are advised to check their passports before departure.
tip: "are advised" is the stress unit, then "to check".

text: The committee will publish its findings at the end of March.
Fewer people now cycle to work because the new lanes are safer.
tip: The reason clause follows "because" without a pause.

text: Please note that all tickets must be collected within seven days.
tip: "Please note that" is one opening unit.

text: The bridge was built in eighteen ninety-eight and is still in daily use.
tip: Say the year smoothly: eighteen ninety-eight.
